name: Norfolk Island separate immigration control (Immigration Act 1980 (NI))
scope: Norfolk Island
rule: Entry and stay on Norfolk Island required a Norfolk Island permit, even for Australian citizens; an Australian visa did not cover the island.
start_quote: On 1 July 2016, the Norfolk Island Immigration Act 1980 was repealed and the Australian migration zone has extended to include Norfolk Island.
end_quote: From 1 July 2016, the Australian migration system replaced the immigration arrangements previously maintained by the Norfolk Island Government.
in_force_quote: Travel between Norfolk Island and mainland Australia became domestic travel on 1 July 2016.
found_via: own lead (abolished separate immigration regimes); web search: Norfolk Island Immigration Act 1980 repealed
notes: WEAK START: the start year is only the year in the title of the repealed Act; its commencement date and earlier immigration ordinances were not read. Started before 2000, ended 2016. Official pages (infrastructure.gov.au, humanrights.gov.au) blocked the fetch.

name: Torres Strait Protected Zone traditional visits (free movement without passports)
scope: Torres Strait Protected Zone islands (and 13 PNG treaty villages)
rule: Traditional inhabitants of listed PNG villages may visit the Protected Zone without passport or visa for traditional activities.
start_quote: The Torres Strait Treaty was signed in December 1978 and entered into force in February 1985.
end_quote: That free movement, confined to a protected zone, was suspended in March 2020 and did not resume when Australia opened its borders to international travel in November last year.
resumed_quote: As a result, and following meetings with relevant stakeholders, traditional travel under the Torres Strait Treaty resumed on 19 October 2022.
expiry_quote: The Torres Strait Treaty was signed in December 1978 and entered into force in February 1985.
in_force_quote: They can make traditional visits (free movement without passports) into the Protected Zone.
found_via: seed; web search: Torres Strait Treaty traditional visits suspended 2020 resumed
notes: Started before 2000; included for its COVID suspension (2.5 years) and resumption. DFAT page read via Wayback (snapshot date not checked), so 'in force 2026' is as of that snapshot. 'Open-ended' is inferred from its being a treaty with no term quoted.

name: Azerbaijan: permit-based access for foreigners to the 'liberated territories'
scope: Shusha, Lachin, Aghdam, Fuzuli, Khojaly, Khankendi (Karabakh / East Zangezur)
rule: Foreign nationals may visit the listed territories individually by car or in organised groups only with a permit (Yolumuz Qarabağa portal, hotel booking or licensed tour).
start_quote: Beginning July 23, 2025, foreign nationals will be permitted to visit the liberated territories of the Republic of Azerbaijan - including Shusha, Lachin, Aghdam, Fuzuli, Khojaly, and Khankendi - either individually by private vehicle or as part of organized groups, provided they obtain the necessary permits. This was announced in a joint statement by the Ministry of Digital Development and Transport and the State Tourism Agency.
notes: azerbaijan.az (official state portal) relaying the joint statement of the Ministry of Digital Development and Transport and the State Tourism Agency. Before this date foreigners had no general access; no pilot/expiry wording in the text. 2026 status not sourced.

name: Nakhchivan visa exemption for Iranian citizens
scope: Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic
rule: Iranian ordinary-passport holders may stay up to 15 days in Nakhchivan without a visa; other regions of Azerbaijan require a visa.
start_quote: “The visa requirement for Iranian citizens holding ordinary passports will be canceled from December 1, 2019, for a stay of up to 15 days,” Iran’s Consulate General said in a statement. This information was confirmed by the Azerbaijani Foreign Ministry. Iranian citizens are required a visa to stay in other Azerbaijani regions.
notes: Trend 2019-11-27 and Azernews 2019-11-28, both citing Iran's Consulate General in Nakhchivan, 'confirmed by the Azerbaijani Foreign Ministry'; no Azerbaijani legal text fetched. No stated expiry in the reports. Status after the 2020 land-border closure and in 2026 not sourced (the pinned Wikipedia 'Visa policy of Azerbaijan' does not mention Nakhchivan).

name: Bangladesh: home ministry permission for foreigners visiting the Chittagong Hill Tracts (January 2015 circular)
scope: Chittagong Hill Tracts (Rangamati, Bandarban, Khagrachhari districts)
rule: All foreign nationals had to apply to the home ministry at least a month before visiting the CHT (previously only district-administration permission).
start_quote: Before the January circular was issued, foreigners needed permission only from the district administration and there was no timeframe for submitting the applications. On the contrary, the January circular made it mandatory for all foreign nationals to submit an application to the home ministry at least a month before the intended visit.
end_quote: "We have withdrawn the circular that was issued recently. From now on, the foreign tourists will be able to visit the CHT districts just like before by seeking permission from the district administration," Asaduzzaman told The Daily Star.
found_via: search: Bangladesh Chittagong Hill Tracts foreigners permission restriction 2015 home ministry
notes: Daily Star, 1 April 2015 (year from the article date): decision taken at a home ministry meeting 'on Sunday' (= 29 March 2015, derived). The underlying district-administration permission for foreigners pre-dates and survives the circular (no sourced start; not a row). Foreign researchers still need ministry permission (20 days ahead). At publication the districts had not yet received the withdrawal. 2026 status not checked.

name: Bhutan: 24-hour SDF waiver in designated border-town zones
scope: Designated zones of the border towns Samtse, Phuentsholing, Gelephu and Samdrup Jongkhar
rule: Casual visitors and tourists of all nationalities may stay up to 24 hours in the border towns without paying the Sustainable Development Fee, if they do not go beyond the designated zone.
start_quote: The Royal Government of Bhutan vide Public Notifications; S-20/2023/385 and S20/2023/387 dated March 30, 2023 has approved the waiver of Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) for casual visitors including tourists of all nationalities for visits upto 24 hours in the border towns of Samtse, Phuentsholing, Gelephu and SamdrupJongkhar as long as they do not travel beyond the designated zone of the border towns. The SDF waiver has been approved for a period of one year with effect from 14 April 2023.
expiry_quote: The SDF waiver has been approved for a period of one year with effect from 14 April 2023. This waiver was further extended for another year via the Cabinet Order number C-3/8(7)/2024/64 dated April 9, 2024.
in_force_quote: 3. The 24 hours SDF waiver for tourists staying in the border towns shall continue. The above incentives will come into effect from 1 September 2023 and shall remain effective for four years till 31 August 2027.
found_via: search: Bhutan border towns 24 hours SDF waiver 2024
notes: A fee-based entry condition, not a visa/permit (kind 'other'). One-year measure from 14 April 2023, extended one year by Cabinet Order of 9 April 2024 (SOP valid till 13 April 2025); the tourism department's announcement on SDF incentives (effective 1 Sept 2023 to 31 Aug 2027) says the waiver 'shall continue'. No end found; the extension after 13 April 2025 rests only on that incentives text.

name: Bhutan: free movement of Indian citizens limited to border towns
scope: Border towns of Phuentsholing, Gelephu and Samdrup Jongkhar
rule: Indian citizens may move freely only within the border towns; travel beyond them requires a permit.
start_quote: From 23 September 2022, this freedom of movement is now restricted to travel within the border towns of Phuentsholing, Gelephu, and Samdrup Jongkhar. Travel beyond these border towns will require a permit, which can be obtained on arrival.
in_force_quote: From 23 September 2022, this freedom of movement is now restricted to travel within the border towns of Phuentsholing, Gelephu, and Samdrup Jongkhar.
notes: Only the Wikipedia sentence (pinned revision, read 2026-10-03) supports both start and current status; no Bhutanese official text for this rule was fetched.

name: Brest / Belovezhskaya Pushcha visa-free zone
scope: Belovezhskaya Pushcha National Park, later Brest city and listed districts of Brest Region
rule: Foreign tourists may enter and stay in the zone without a visa for a limited number of days.
start_quote: The legislation superseded the previous decrees that established two separate visa-free zones: Brest area including Belovezhskaya Pushcha National Park (since June 2015) and Augustów Canal area including Grodno (since October 2016).
in_force_quote: Since November 2019, citizens that qualify for the visa-free program through the Minsk National Airport may visit a visa-free zone in the Brest Region and the Grodno Region for 15 days without a visa.
notes: Merged in November 2019 into one Brest-Grodno visa-free territory (15 days); recorded as continuing, not ended - the merger widened the same regional exemption. Wikipedia only; belarus.by not read in this session. Consistent with the seed ('2015/2016 separate zones; merged 2019-11'). The June 2015 zone is understood to have been the national park only at first - unverified.

name: Augustów Canal / Grodno visa-free zone
scope: Augustów Canal park, Grodno city and listed districts of Grodno Region
rule: Foreign tourists may enter and stay in the zone without a visa for a limited number of days.
start_quote: The legislation superseded the previous decrees that established two separate visa-free zones: Brest area including Belovezhskaya Pushcha National Park (since June 2015) and Augustów Canal area including Grodno (since October 2016).
in_force_quote: Since November 2019, citizens that qualify for the visa-free program through the Minsk National Airport may visit a visa-free zone in the Brest Region and the Grodno Region for 15 days without a visa.
notes: Merged in November 2019 into one Brest-Grodno visa-free territory (15 days); recorded as continuing, not ended - the merger widened the same regional exemption. Wikipedia only; belarus.by not read in this session. Consistent with the seed ('2015/2016 separate zones; merged 2019-11'). The June 2015 zone is understood to have been the national park only at first - unverified.

name: Latvia-Belarus local border traffic zone
scope: Border areas of Belarus and Latvia
rule: Border-area residents with a local border traffic permit may visit the other side's border area without a visa.
start_quote: As of June 2017 [update] , ten local-traffic agreements have come into force. Hungary–Ukraine from January 2008. Slovakia–Ukraine from September 2008. Poland–Ukraine in July 2009. Romania–Moldova from October 2010. Latvia–Belarus from February 2012. Norway–Russia from May 2012. Poland–Russia (Kaliningrad Area) from July 2012 (suspended since July 2016) Latvia–Russia from June 2013.
found_via: enwiki 'Schengen Area', list of local border traffic agreements
notes: Start date conflict inside Wikipedia: 'Visa policy of the Schengen Area' says 'Belarus (with Latvia since 2011)', 'Schengen Area' says 'Latvia–Belarus from February 2012'. Current status not established (no source read). Applies to border residents only.

name: Rapa Nui residence and stay law (Ley 21.070)
scope: Easter Island (Rapa Nui)
rule: Any Chilean or foreign visitor may stay at most 30 days and must file an entry form; longer stay only for listed categories.
start_quote: A partir de este 1 de Agosto comienza a regir la nueva Ley de Residencia y Permanencia en Rapa Nui, la que pretende revertir el daño causado por el explosivo aumento de su población.
expiry_quote: Por esta razón, es que de ahora en adelante, los turistas que viajen a Rapa Nui podrán mantenerse por un plazo de 30 días como máximo.
notes: Chilean Interior Ministry news item of 2018-08-01. Open-ended ('de ahora en adelante'). No source fetched for 2026 status (a search result of Sept 2026 about abuses of the residence law suggests it is in force - not quoted). COVID closure of the island 2020-2022 not researched.

name: 15-day visa-free entry for foreign cruise tour groups (Shanghai pilot, later all cruise ports)
scope: Beijing and 11 coastal provincial-level units (originally entry via Shanghai cruise terminals only)
rule: Foreign tour groups of two or more arriving by cruise ship and received by a Chinese travel agency may stay 15 days without a visa, only within Beijing and the listed coastal provinces.
start_quote: Non visa-exempt citizens traveling with tour groups on cruise ships may enter China without a visa for a maximum stay of 15 days since 1 October 2016
end_quote: Policies including port visas, 24/72/144-hour visa-free transit policy, Hainan 30-day visa-free policy, 15-day visa-free policy specified for foreign cruise-group-tour through Shanghai Port, Guangdong 144-hour visa-free policy specified for foreign tour groups from Hong Kong or Macao SAR, and Guangxi 15-day visa-free policy specified for foreign tour groups of ASEAN countries will also be temporarily suspended.
resumed_quote: Resuming Hainan visa-free policy, visa-free policy specified for foreign cruise-group-tour through Shanghai Port, Guangdong visa-free policy specified for foreign tour groups from Hong Kong or Macao SAR, and Guangxi visa-free policy specified for foreign tour groups of ASEAN countries
expiry_quote: Shanghai has been piloting China's visa-free policy for cruise tourists since October 2016, leading to a 10 percent average annual increase in the number of cruise passengers.
in_force_quote: may enter China without a visa by a cruise ship via one of the cruise ports in the following 13 cities
notes: Exact start day (1 October 2016) is from Wikipedia only; gov.cn/China Daily (2024-05-16) confirms 'since October 2016' and calls it a pilot, retrospectively - no 2016 text was read. Expanded from Shanghai to cruise ports in 13 cities on Wednesday 2024-05-15 ('announced and implemented on Wednesday', article of May 16, 2024). Suspension: MFA/NIA announcement of 2020-03-26 (embassy copy), 'effective from 0 a.m., 28 march 2020'. Resumption: MFA notice of 2023-03-14, 'China would implement the following policies from 15 March 2023'.

name: Guangdong 144-hour visa-free entry for foreign tour groups from Hong Kong and Macao
scope: Ten Guangdong cities (Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Foshan, Dongguan, Zhongshan, Jiangmen, Zhaoqing, Huizhou, Shantou)
rule: Foreign tour groups organised by a Hong Kong or Macao travel agency may stay 6 days without a visa, only within the ten listed cities.
start_quote: the “144-hour Convenient Visa” policy has been launched since 2000, offering simplified procedures to visitors who enter Guangdong province via 10 entry ports
end_quote: Policies including port visas, 24/72/144-hour visa-free transit policy, Hainan 30-day visa-free policy, 15-day visa-free policy specified for foreign cruise-group-tour through Shanghai Port, Guangdong 144-hour visa-free policy specified for foreign tour groups from Hong Kong or Macao SAR, and Guangxi 15-day visa-free policy specified for foreign tour groups of ASEAN countries will also be temporarily suspended.
resumed_quote: Resuming Hainan visa-free policy, visa-free policy specified for foreign cruise-group-tour through Shanghai Port, Guangdong visa-free policy specified for foreign tour groups from Hong Kong or Macao SAR, and Guangxi visa-free policy specified for foreign tour groups of ASEAN countries
in_force_quote: The foreign tourists in this case can stay for a maximum of 6 days in the following cities: Dongguan, Foshan, Guangzhou, Huizhou, Jiangmen, Shantou, Shenzhen, Zhaoqing, Zhongshan and Zhuhai.
notes: Start year rests on the Hong Kong Tourism Board trade page only (undated page; a search snippet said 'November 2000', not confirmed in fetched text). Whether the 2000 scheme already covered all ten cities was not established. No Chinese primary text for the start was read. Suspension: MFA/NIA announcement of 2020-03-26 (embassy copy), 'effective from 0 a.m., 28 march 2020'. Resumption: MFA notice of 2023-03-14, 'China would implement the following policies from 15 March 2023'.

name: Guilin 6-day visa-free entry for ASEAN tour groups
scope: Guilin (prefecture-level city), Guangxi
rule: Tour groups from the ten ASEAN states entering and leaving through Guilin airport may stay 6 days without a visa, only within Guilin.
start_quote: will offer six-day visa-free entry to group tourists from the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) starting Thursday
end_quote: Policies including port visas, 24/72/144-hour visa-free transit policy, Hainan 30-day visa-free policy, 15-day visa-free policy specified for foreign cruise-group-tour through Shanghai Port, Guangdong 144-hour visa-free policy specified for foreign tour groups from Hong Kong or Macao SAR, and Guangxi 15-day visa-free policy specified for foreign tour groups of ASEAN countries will also be temporarily suspended.
resumed_quote: Resuming Hainan visa-free policy, visa-free policy specified for foreign cruise-group-tour through Shanghai Port, Guangdong visa-free policy specified for foreign tour groups from Hong Kong or Macao SAR, and Guangxi visa-free policy specified for foreign tour groups of ASEAN countries
in_force_quote: can stay within the administrative region of Guilin, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region for a maximum of 6 days
notes: Start day derived: Xinhua/China Daily article dated Wednesday 2015-05-27 says 'starting Thursday' (= 2015-05-28). The 2020 suspension and 2023 resumption notices name a 'Guangxi 15-day visa-free policy ... for foreign tour groups of ASEAN countries', not a 6-day Guilin one - an unresolved mismatch of wording (stay length); it is taken here as the same scheme because no other Guangxi ASEAN-group scheme was found. Suspension: MFA/NIA announcement of 2020-03-26 (embassy copy), 'effective from 0 a.m., 28 march 2020'. Resumption: MFA notice of 2023-03-14, 'China would implement the following policies from 15 March 2023'.

name: Hainan 144-hour visa-free entry for foreign tour groups from Hong Kong and Macao
scope: Hainan Province
rule: Foreign tour groups of two or more organised by a Hong Kong or Macao travel agency may enter Hainan from the SARs without a visa for 144 hours and must stay within the province.
start_quote: The eligible foreign nationals may enter and exit in groups through any of the exit-entry ports set up by the State in Hainan Province, and shall stay within the administrative region of Hainan. The duration of stay for each foreign national is calculated from 0:00 on the day following the day of entry. The announcement is hereby made. National Immigration Administration July 30, 2024
in_force_quote: The tourists concerned shall enter and exit the Hainan Province as part of their tourist group via any of the exit-entry ports in Hainan and can stay for a maximum of 6 days.
notes: NIA Announcement No. 8 (2024): 'Effective from the release date of this announcement'; the announcement is dated July 30, 2024. No pilot or expiry wording in the announcement, but nothing states open-endedness either.

name: Hainan visa-free entry (group scheme 2000, 59-country scheme 2018)
scope: Hainan Province
rule: Ordinary-passport holders of listed countries (61 in 2026) may enter Hainan without a visa for up to 30 days and must stay within the province.
start_quote: Hainan has offered a 15-day visa-free stay for group tourists from 21 countries since 2000, and added another five countries to the list in 2010.
end_quote: Policies including port visas, 24/72/144-hour visa-free transit policy, Hainan 30-day visa-free policy, 15-day visa-free policy specified for foreign cruise-group-tour through Shanghai Port, Guangdong 144-hour visa-free policy specified for foreign tour groups from Hong Kong or Macao SAR, and Guangxi 15-day visa-free policy specified for foreign tour groups of ASEAN countries will also be temporarily suspended.
resumed_quote: Resuming Hainan visa-free policy, visa-free policy specified for foreign cruise-group-tour through Shanghai Port, Guangdong visa-free policy specified for foreign tour groups from Hong Kong or Macao SAR, and Guangxi visa-free policy specified for foreign tour groups of ASEAN countries
in_force_quote: Foreign nationals holding ordinary passports from 61 countries may enter and stay within the administrative region of Hainan Province for a maximum of 30 days without a visa
notes: Start (2000, 21 countries, groups, 15 days) and the 2010 addition rest on Xinhua 2018-04-18 only; the same article announces the widening to 59 countries, individuals and 30 days 'from May 1' 2018. Suspension, resumption and 2026 status are primary (MFA/NIA; NIA page dated 2026-08-20). Suspension: MFA/NIA announcement of 2020-03-26 (embassy copy), 'effective from 0 a.m., 28 march 2020'. Resumption: MFA notice of 2023-03-14, 'China would implement the following policies from 15 March 2023'. Seed says 2010 for the group scheme; Xinhua says since 2000 with five countries added in 2010.

name: 72/144/240-hour visa-free transit with a permitted-stay area
scope: Listed cities/provinces per port of entry (Beijing and Shanghai in 2013; 24 provincial-level units, some partial, since 2024-12)
rule: Nationals of listed countries in transit to a third country may enter without a visa for 72 h (later 144 h, now 240 h) but must stay inside the area permitted for their port of entry.
start_quote: Starting from 1 January 2013, holders of passports issued by the following countries do not need a visa if transiting through Beijing Capital International Airport in Beijing, Shanghai Pudong International Airport and Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport
end_quote: Policies including port visas, 24/72/144-hour visa-free transit policy, Hainan 30-day visa-free policy, 15-day visa-free policy specified for foreign cruise-group-tour through Shanghai Port, Guangdong 144-hour visa-free policy specified for foreign tour groups from Hong Kong or Macao SAR, and Guangxi 15-day visa-free policy specified for foreign tour groups of ASEAN countries will also be temporarily suspended.
resumed_quote: Third, resume the issuance of port visa, the implementation of the 24/72/144-hour visa-free transit policy, and the issuance of temporary entry permit in accordance with the law.
in_force_quote: may enter visa-free through any of the designated 65 open exit-entry ports in 24 provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government and stay in the permitted areas for no more than 10 days
notes: Recorded as one regime. Resumption: NIA announcement dated 2022-12-27, measures 'starting from January 8, 2023'. Later changes of detail: 144 h for Shanghai/Jiangsu/Zhejiang 'Since 30 January 2016' (Wikipedia revision of 2020-01, oldid 935456644); on 2024-12-17 the stay was 'extended from the previous 72 hours and 144 hours to 240 hours' and areas widened to 24 provinces (NIA English news item c178106 is dated 2024-12-19 and says 'announced today'; the date 17 December 2024 is from the Wikipedia citation of the Chinese NIA notice). So the 72/144-hour variants ended by replacement with a wider regional rule, not by abolition.

name: Xishuangbanna 6-day visa-free entry for ASEAN tour groups
scope: Xishuangbanna Dai Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan
rule: Tour groups of two or more from ASEAN states may enter via Xishuangbanna airport or the Mohan rail/road ports and stay 6 days without a visa, only within the prefecture.
start_quote: Please note that the travel only limited to the administrative region of Xishuangbanna Dai Autonomous Prefecture in Yunnan Province and the stay shall not exceed six days, with the duration starting at 00:00 on the day following entry. Those eligible under mutual visa exemption agreements with China or China's unilateral visa exemption policy may follow the applicable regulations. Announcement is hereby given. National Immigration Administration February 10, 2025
in_force_quote: can stay within the administrative region of Xishuangbanna Dai Autonomous Prefecture for a maximum of 6 days
notes: NIA Announcement No. 1 [2025], effective 'As of today' (dated February 10, 2025). No pilot/expiry wording.

name: Colombia Tarjeta de Movilidad Fronteriza (TMF) for Venezuelans
scope: Designated Colombian municipalities bordering Venezuela
rule: Venezuelans resident in the border zone may enter and move only within designated border municipalities with the card instead of a passport.
start_quote: Esta medida, que entra en vigencia desde el 1o. de mayo, se toma con el fin de facilitar la movilidad y de garantizar una frontera segura y ordenada.
end_quote: El presidente colombiano Juan Manuel Santos anunció este 08 de febrero las medidas que tomarán para solucionar el actual conflicto que se presenta en la frontera con Venezuela, debido a la migración masiva.
resumed_quote: "Con la reapertura de la Tarjeta de Movilidad Fronteriza se busca evitar que los ciudadanos venezolanos hagan su tránsito a Colombia por pasos no regulados
found_via: own lead; web search: Tarjeta de Movilidad Fronteriza suspendida 2018
notes: What was suspended in Feb 2018 is the ISSUANCE of new cards ('se dejará de emitir la Tarjeta de Movilidad Fronteriza (TMF) para venezolanos' - Panorama 2018-02-09, via Wayback); cards already issued stayed usable per the same article, so this is a partial suspension. Reopened Nov 2018 (Infobae article dated 28 Nov 2018; a search snippet says 21 Nov). Border closures 2019 and 2020-2021 and the card's status in 2026 were not researched (a Dec 2021 article saved as C_cronica_tmf says the card was again required from 6 Dec 2021).

name: Algeria: regularisation visa on arrival for organised tourism in the Great South
scope: Southern wilayas (initially about a dozen, now 24)
rule: Foreign tourists travelling to the southern wilayas through an approved Algerian agency get a visa on arrival (max 30 days) instead of a consular visa.
start_quote: Le ministère de l’Intérieur a annoncé ce dispositif en décembre 2022, quelques jours avant l’inauguration du vol Paris – Djanet.
expiry_quote: The Algerian authorities have decided, within the framework of the promotion and facilitation of Saharan tourism, to set up, on an exceptional and temporary basis, and in substitution for consular visas, regularization visas (visa upon arrival), for foreign tourists who choose the Great South of Algeria as a tourist destination.
in_force_quote: À l’approche de la saison touristique saharienne 2026-2027, l’Algérie maintient son visa à l’arrivée pour les touristes étrangers qui visitent le Sud par l’intermédiaire d’une agence de voyages agréée.
notes: 'Exceptional and temporary' wording is primary (Algerian embassy in Budapest; same in French on the Astana embassy page) but undated (footer 2023); no end date was ever stated. Start month from Algérie360 (2026-09-28), which also reports the scheme renewed for the 2026-2027 season in 24 wilayas. Embassy in Brussels lists 12 wilayas; Wikipedia says the government proposed in Dec 2024 to extend it to all provinces (not verified).

name: Eritrea: travel permits for foreigners outside Asmara
scope: All of Eritrea outside Asmara
rule: Foreign nationals need a government travel permit for any travel outside the capital.
start_quote: The Eritrean government restricts the travel of foreigners outside of Asmara via a 2006 decree. While it has granted requests for travel to Keren, Mendefera, and Massawa, access is not guaranteed.
in_force_quote: Foreign nationals require a government-issued travel permit to travel between regions. Always carry identification If you are travelling outside Asmara, have your mandatory travel permits with you
notes: Start year from the US OSAC country security report ('a 2006 decree'); the decree itself not found. In force per Government of Canada travel advice fetched 2026-10-03. Inverse scope (everything except the capital).

name: Ceuta and Melilla visa exemption for residents of Tetouan and Nador provinces
scope: Ceuta and Melilla
rule: Moroccans resident in the adjacent provinces (Tetouan for Ceuta, Nador for Melilla) could enter the city without a visa, but not continue to the rest of Spain.
start_quote: This system is older and was included in the 1991 accession treaty of Spain to the Schengen Area.
end_quote: The European Schengen Agreement excluded the residents of the Tetouan and Nador regions from having to obtain a visa, but the Spanish government suspended this exception in May 2021
notes: One row for both cities (one rule). Started before 2000. End date conflict: Middle East Monitor (2023-02-15) dates the suspension to May 2021, while the land border had already been closed from March 2020 (seed note: 'de facto suspension after 2020'; closure date not quoted here), so the regime stopped operating earlier than the quoted date. The same article reports Spain calling the change 'irreversible'; no source read on 2026 status, and the pinned enwiki 'Special territories' page still mentions the exemption arrangements in the present tense.

name: Saint-Georges-de-l'Oyapock / Oiapoque cross-border circulation regime (carte de frontalier)
scope: Commune of Saint-Georges-de-l'Oyapock, French Guiana (and Oiapoque, Brazil)
rule: Residents of Oiapoque holding a border card may stay in Saint-Georges up to 72 hours without the visa otherwise required for French Guiana.
start_quote: le régime de « circulation frontalière » institué par échange de lettres entre le Brésil et la France, est entré en vigueur le 12 juin 2014.
end_quote: L’émission de la carte transfrontalière entre Saint-Georges et Oiapoque a été interrompue pendant la période de crise Covid.
resumed_quote: La suspension aura duré 4 ans et depuis ce 18 janvier, les services préfectoraux traitent les nouvelles demandes et les renouvellements.
found_via: own lead; web search: Oiapoque Saint-Georges carte de frontalier
notes: Start from a French Senate report (primary); cards were issued from 2015-01-01 ('Le dispositif de délivrance de cartes frontalières a été lancé le 1 er janvier 2015'). Suspension year 2020 is derived from 'crise Covid' + 'aura duré 4 ans' (La 1ère, 2024-01-24) - the exact date is not given, and what was suspended is the ISSUANCE of cards. French Guiana has its own ISO code (GF); the regime covers one commune of it. Applies to border residents only. No 2026 source.

name: Greece 'Visa Express' for Turkish citizens on Eastern Aegean islands
scope: Lesvos, Chios, Samos, Kos, Rhodes, Kalymnos, Limnos, Leros, Symi, Kastelorizo (later also Patmos, Samothrace per search result, not quoted)
rule: Turkish citizens get a 7-day visa on arrival valid only for the island of entry, not for the rest of Greece/Schengen.
start_quote: The program has been in effect on the Eastern Aegean islands since April 2024 , introduced during Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis’ visit to Lesvos after a proposal by regional authorities.
expiry_quote: “The renewal of the Visa Express program for another year is a particularly positive development for the economy of the North Aegean islands,” said North Aegean Governor Konstantinos Moutzouris.
in_force_quote: Greece has extended its Visa Express program until April 2027, allowing Turkish citizens to travel more easily to the Eastern Aegean islands through a fast-track visa-on-arrival process.
notes: Trade-press article (GTP, 2026-04-01) read via the Wayback Machine. 'Stated expiry' is inferred from yearly renewals ('for another year', 'until April 2027'); the original 2024 decision and its term were not read. Greek MFA text not read.

name: Greece visa-facilitation pilot for visitors from Turkey to Eastern Aegean islands
scope: Rhodes, Kos, Samos, Chios, Lesvos (later also Symi, Kastelorizo)
rule: Turkish and other non-EU visitors arriving from Turkey could get a short-stay visa at the island port, valid for the island visit (under 15 days).
start_quote: hailed the visa facilitation pilot program launched last month that allows Turkish nationals to visit five Greek Eastern Aegean islands without a relevant visa issued at Greek consulates.
expiry_quote: The pilot program will end on 30 September 2012.
found_via: web search: Greece pilot programme 2012 Turkish tourists visa islands (looking for the predecessor of the 2024 scheme)
notes: A pilot with a stated end (30 Sep 2012) that was renewed for years: NewGreekTV 2016-05-26 ('will be extended for one year') and SchengenVisaInfo 2018-04-18 ('the European Union has decided to extend for another year the visa facilitation program') - both saved. Post was dated 1 Jul 2012, so 'last month' = June 2012; a search snippet of the Greek MFA page says 7 June 2012 (page not fetchable). Whether and when the pilot ended, and its relation to the 2024 'Visa Express' (separate row), were not established.

name: Visa-free visits to Batam, Bintan and Karimun for Singapore permanent residents
scope: Batam island, Bintan island and Karimun regency (Riau Islands)
rule: Foreign holders of Singapore permanent residence may enter Batam, Bintan and Karimun without a visa for up to 4 days.
start_quote: The Jokowi administration signed the Presidential Regulation 95/2024 on 29 August 2024, which resumed visa-free access to tourists from Colombia , Hong Kong , and Suriname , as well as granting visa-free entry to Batam , Bintan and Karimun in the Riau Islands for Singapore permanent resident holders up to four days.
notes: 2024-08-29 is the signing of Perpres 95/2024 (Wikipedia; the regulation text was not read). Operational start was later: Directorate General of Immigration press release of 8 Okt 2024 (https://www.imigrasi.go.id/siaran_pers/2024/10/08/silmy-karim-tarik-wisatawan-asing-imigrasi-berikan-bebas-visa-kunjungan-ke-batam-bintan-dan-karimun-bagi-pemegang-pr-singapur) announces the policy via Circular IMI-940.GR.01.01 Tahun 2024, 'masa tinggal paling lama 4 (empat) hari', entry through listed ferry terminals. No 2026 status source read. Earlier Riau Islands special visa-on-arrival schemes: nothing sourced.

name: Andaman & Nicobar: islands excluded from the Restricted Area Permit regime
scope: 30 (later listed as 29) inhabited islands of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands
rule: Foreigners (except citizens/origin of Afghanistan, China, Pakistan) may visit the listed islands without a Restricted Area Permit.
start_quote: The Restricted Area Permit (RAP) regime notified under the Foreigners (Restricted Area) Order, 1963 has been relaxed vide Circular No. 506 of Foreigners Division, MHA, GOI dated 29.6.2018 and subsequently issued vide Circular No. 514 dated 17.09.2018 in Andaman & Nicobar Islands for 30 inhabited islands, requirement of RAP has been done with i.e no RAP is required by a foreigners to visit these islands, till 31.12.2022.
expiry_quote: requirement of RAP has been done with i.e no RAP is required by a foreigners to visit these islands, till 31.12.2022.
in_force_quote: The foreign nationals are not required to obtain a Restricted Area Permit (RAP) for visiting the 29 islands in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands that have been excluded from the RAP regime. Additionally, 11 islands have been exempted from the RAP requirement for day visits only, and this exemption is valid up to 31/12/2027.
notes: Start date is the date of MHA circular No. 506 (29.6.2018; re-issued as No. 514 of 17.09.2018) as quoted by A&N Police (page fetched from web.archive.org; snapshot date not checked). Stated expiry 31.12.2022 passed without an end: the A&N Tourism document (file name dated 2026-03-05) still lists 29 islands as excluded from RAP and adds 11 islands exempt for day visits until 31/12/2027. The extension instrument itself was not found; 30 vs 29 islands is a discrepancy between the two official texts.

name: Ladakh Inner Line Permit for Indian citizens (2017 reinstatement)
scope: Notified protected areas of Ladakh (Leh district: Nubra, Pangong, Tso Moriri, Dah-Hanu etc.)
rule: Indian citizens from outside needed an Inner Line Permit to enter the protected areas of Ladakh.
start_quote: An ILP was previously required for certain parts of the Leh district in Ladakh . This requirement was abolished by a circular issued by the district magistrate which took effect from 1 May 2014, although foreign nationals are required to get Protected Area Permit for this region. The ILP was implemented again in 2017 only to be removed again in 2021.
end_quote: Indian nationals travelling to Ladakh will no longer have to secure an inner line permit. In a bid to welcome tourists, the administration of the Union Territory has now done away with the mandatory permit for entry into the notified protected areas in the interior part of the Union Territory.
found_via: search: Ladakh inner line permit abolished Indian citizens August 2021
notes: Applies to domestic (Indian) visitors; foreigners still need a Protected Area Permit. Wikipedia (pinned revision) gives the sequence: older ILP abolished with effect from 1 May 2014, implemented again in 2017, removed again in 2021. End dated by Free Press Journal article updated 2021-08-07 (search results name a notification of 6 August 2021, not quoted from a saved text). 2017 start has only the Wikipedia sentence. 2026 status not checked: travel sites still advertise a 'Ladakh ILP' in 2026, unverified.

name: Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland excluded from the Protected Area regime
scope: Whole of Manipur, Mizoram and Nagaland
rule: Foreigners (except citizens/origin of Afghanistan, China, Pakistan) could visit the three states without a Protected Area Permit, registering with the FRO within 24 hours.
start_quote: As per instructions issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs on 30.12.2010, the entire area of the States of Manipur, Mizoram and Nagaland has been excluded from the Protected Area regime notified under the Foreigners (Protected Areas) Order 1958, initially for a period of one year w.e.f. 1.1.2011, which has been extended from time to time.
end_quote: In a recent letter, Mr Rio said that the renewed PAP restrictions, which was re-imposed from 17 December 2024 for Nagaland, Manipur, and Mizoram over security concerns, are unnecessary for Nagaland and could harm its growing tourism sector.
expiry_quote: initially for a period of one year w.e.f. 1.1.2011, which has been extended from time to time. This relaxation has been extended till 31.12.2022
in_force_quote: The Chief Minister highlighted that the State Cabinet had discussed the issue multiple times, and repeatedly written to the Ministry of Home Affairs since January 2025 requesting him to restore the earlier PAP relaxations.
notes: Start/expiry: MHA Annex VII (mha.gov.in, primary). End: Akashvani/newsonair (state broadcaster) 2025-11-19 dates the re-imposition 17 December 2024 for all three states together; PTI via National Herald (2024-12-19) confirms via Manipur government statement; the MHA order itself was not fetched. One-year relaxation was rolled over for 14 years (to 31.12.2012, ..., to 31.12.2022; PTI/Gulf News 2018 reports a five-year extension from 1 April 2018); the extension covering 2023-2024 was not sourced. Latest read status is Nov 2025 (Nagaland asking for restoration); no 2026 source on whether it was restored.

name: Kurdistan Region of Iraq: own e-visa portal
scope: Kurdistan Region of Iraq
rule: Visitors to the Kurdistan Region obtain a KRG e-visa (visit.gov.krd) or KRG visa on arrival, separate from the federal Iraqi visa.
start_quote: Kurdistan Region Prime Minister Masrour Barzani on Wednesday, February 22 announced the launch of the KRG’s first e-Visa portal, in line with the promise to turn KRG into a digital government powerhouse by the end of 2025.
in_force_quote: In order to travel to the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, you need an e-Visa. If you are from Country List A , you only need to apply for an e-Visa in one of the following ways: Through the E-VISA portal (visit.gov.krd): You can apply for a Visit or Tourist visa and get an e-Visa within a few minutes.
notes: Start = launch of the portal (gov.krd; year 2023 from the page URL /posts/2023/february/); a separate KRG visa-on-arrival existed before (start unsourced). CONTRADICTION with the lead of a 2025 merger: the pinned Wikipedia 'Visa policy of Iraq' says both that 'As of September 2025' the federal e-Visa portal is 'solely responsible' and that Iraqi Kurdistan 'has its own eVisa platform'; visit.gov.krd and gov.krd visitor pages fetched on 2026-10-03 still offer the KRG e-visa, and the KRG Interior Ministry denied changes on 2025-02-20 (Kurdistan Chronicle). No source for an end was found, so no end is recorded.

name: Multiple-entry tourist visa for Chinese individuals tied to a stay in Okinawa
scope: Okinawa Prefecture (condition of first visit)
rule: Chinese individual tourists with sufficient means get a 3-year multiple-entry visa on condition that they stay at least one night in Okinawa on the first visit.
start_quote: The Government has decided that from July 1 we will begin issuing multiple entry visas to visit Okinawa to Chinese individuals and their families on the basis that those individuals have sufficient economic means.
notes: Borderline case: the visa admits to all Japan; only the condition is regional. Year 2011 comes from the date of the press conference (May 27, 2011). Still listed on the MOFA page 'Visa information for Chinese nationals' dated September 28, 2022 (archived copy: 'Multiple-entry visas for individual tourists visiting Okinawa / Tohoku Region'), alongside an unconditional multiple-entry visa for higher means - so not folded into the general rule as of 2022; 2026 status not checked (mofa.go.jp blocks curl; archive copy is of 2022). Sister scheme for three Tohoku prefectures (Iwate, Miyagi, Fukushima): no sourced start date found (seed/memory: 2012-07-01), hence no row; MOFA press release of 2017-04-21 widened it to six prefectures from 2017-05-08.

name: Visa-free group visits by Chinese citizens to Tongrim County and Sinuiju
scope: Tongrim County and Sinuiju (North Pyongan)
rule: Chinese ordinary-passport holders in a tour group may stay up to 2 days in Tongrim County, or visit Sinuiju on a day trip, without a visa.
start_quote: Since 2014, citizens of China holding ordinary passports visiting only the Tongrim County in a tour group can stay there for up to 2 days. They may also visit Sinuiju for a day trip without a visa.
found_via: Wikipedia 'Visa policy of North Korea' (seed lead kp-sinuiju)
notes: Weak row: Wikipedia only (it cites China Daily 2014-10-17 and NK News 2015-12-23; the archived China Daily page was not available). North Korea closed its borders to tourism in January 2020 (Koryo Tours blog: 'since closure in January 2020'), which must have interrupted this scheme, but no source specific to Tongrim/Sinuiju was read, so end and 2026 status are empty. Seed says Sinuiju from 2015.

name: Jeju visa-free entry
scope: Jeju Province
rule: Nationals of all countries except those designated by the Minister of Justice may enter Jeju directly without a visa for 30 days and must stay on Jeju unless given permission to extend the sojourn area.
start_quote: Jeju's visa-waiver program was introduced on May 1, 2002, as a part of Special Act on the Development of Jeju International Cosmopolitan City
end_quote: The visa-free entry policy to Jeju which has been suspended since 4 February 2020, to prevent the inflow of COVID19, will resume starting 1 June, 2022.
resumed_quote: The visa-free entry policy to Jeju which has been suspended since 4 February 2020, to prevent the inflow of COVID19, will resume starting 1 June, 2022.
expiry_quote: 제주특별법에 근거한 제주 무사증 입국제도가 별도로 상시 운영되고 있다.
in_force_quote: 제주에서는 일정 국가 국민을 제외한 외국인이 관광·통과 등의 목적으로 입국할 경우 비자 없이 최장 30일간 체류할 수 있는 무사증 입국제도가 운영되고 있다.
notes: Start date is from Wikipedia only (no statute text read); a search snippet mentioned an earlier 15-day Jeju scheme from 1980 - not verified. Suspension and resumption dates are primary (ROK consulate notice; MOJ press release of 2022-05-25 also confirms resumption). 'No stated expiry' rests on a 2026-09-18 Financial News article calling it a permanently operated scheme based on the Jeju Special Act, not on the 2002 text. The same article reports a National Assembly petition (78,800 signatures) in which the Jeju waiver is contested.

name: Muan airport visa-free entry for tour groups
scope: South Jeolla, Gwangju, North Jeolla and Jeju
rule: Tour groups of five or more from Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia arriving at Muan airport may stay 15 days without a visa and travel in South Jeolla, Gwangju, North Jeolla and Jeju.
start_quote: Muan International Airport implemented visa-free entry for group tourists to 3 Asian countries starting from 15 March 2023.
expiry_quote: 제도 운영 기간은 2024년 3월 31일까지 1년이며 시행 결과에 대한 평가를 거쳐 1년 단위로 연장이 가능하다.
notes: The same embassy notice (2024-02-27) says the scheme 'has been extended until March 31, 2025'. No source found for an extension beyond 2025-03-31 or for a formal end; end fields left empty. Context, not an end of the regime: Wikipedia (Muan International Airport, oldid 1377416195) says the airport 'is still closed following the Jeju Air crash. All flights are suspended as of 17 May 2026', so the scheme could not be used in practice since 2024-12-29. Likely lapsed 2025-03-31 - unverified.

name: Yangyang airport visa-free entry for tour groups
scope: Gangwon Province and the Seoul Metropolitan Area
rule: Tour groups from Vietnam, the Philippines, Indonesia (and Mongolia) arriving on the same flight at Yangyang airport may stay 15 days without a visa and travel within the Seoul Metropolitan Area and Gangwon Province with a guide.
start_quote: introduces visa- free entry to 4 Asian countries* for group tourists entering Yangyang Airport from 1 June 2022
expiry_quote: The implementation period is 1 year from 1 June 2022 to 31 May 2023 (1 October 2022 to 31 May 2023 for Mongolia). The period can be extended in 1 year increments after assessment.
notes: Extended at least once more: ROK embassy in Manila notice of 2024-04-02 says the Yangyang scheme 'has been extended until May 31, 2025' (https://overseas.mofa.go.kr/ph-en/brd/m_3275/view.do?seq=760966; that notice gives the start as 15 March 2023, apparently copied from the Muan notice - contradicts the MOJ release). No source found for any extension beyond 2025-05-31 or for a formal end, so end and 2026 status are left empty (unknown, not 'still in force'). Wikipedia (Visa policy of South Korea, oldid 1368085747) still describes it as 'extended once a year'.

name: Sri Lanka: Ministry of Defence prior permission for foreign passport holders travelling to the North
scope: Northern Province (checked at Omanthai)
rule: All foreign passport holders needed prior Ministry of Defence permission to travel to the Northern Province.
start_quote: Meanwhile the Ministry of Defence (MoD) announced on 10 October that all foreign passport holders travelling to the north would require prior permission to do so. Conditions were subsequently relaxed enabling foreign passport holders of Sri Lankan origin to travel without prior permission.
end_quote: The regulations imposed by the Ministry of Defence (MOD) on foreign passport holders traveling to the North have been lifted. The Ministry of Defence said that the decision was taken at the first Security Council meeting of President Maithripala Sirisena. According to the Ministry of Defence it was felt that since there is a peaceful environment in Sri Lanka such regulations will not be required anymore.
in_force_quote: Defence Ministry spokesman Brigadier Ruwan Wanigasooriya in a statement said the National Security Council met under the newly elected President Maithripala Sirisena on Friday and lifted the ban.
notes: Start: UK FCO 'country of concern' update of 31 December 2014 (year from the document title); Malay Mail/AFP 2014-10-13 says the ban had been in place 'since Friday' (= 10 Oct), while Reuters via Gulf News says it was imposed 'on October 15' - contradiction on the start day. End: Daily FT dated Saturday 17 January 2015; Reuters says the National Security Council lifted it 'on Friday' (i.e. 16 Jan 2015, derived, hence month precision). No stated expiry found. An EARLIER version of the same requirement was lifted with effect from 4 July 2011 (Sri Lanka High Commission in India quoting defence.lk, saved as B_lk_slhc) - its start date was not sourced, so no row. The in_force quote is the 2015 lifting, not a 2026 reading.

name: Libya: visa-free entry for Belarusian citizens via Benghazi only
scope: Entry at Benghazi (eastern Libya)
rule: Citizens of Belarus may enter Libya without a visa only when landing at Benghazi.
start_quote: Citizens of Belarus may only land at Benghazi without a visa. Date of visa changes This list is incomplete ; you can help by adding missing items . ( September 2026 ) Introduced: Unknown: Benin 26 May 2025: Belarus
in_force_quote: Citizens of Algeria and Mauritania may only land at Misurata and Tripoli Mitiga without a visa. Citizens of Belarus may only land at Benghazi without a visa.
notes: Wikipedia only (pinned revision read 2026-10-03); the list entry '26 May 2025: Belarus' is in the 'Introduced' list and is read as the date of this exemption. Same page: Algerian and Mauritanian citizens visa-free only at Misurata and Tripoli Mitiga (Mauritania 'restored' 30 August 2026) - a mirror-image west-only exemption, not given its own row because its start date for Algeria is not stated.

name: Gilgit-Baltistan NOC requirement for foreign tourists (2017 enforcement)
scope: Gilgit-Baltistan
rule: Foreign tourists were barred from visiting Gilgit-Baltistan without a no-objection certificate from the federal interior ministry.
start_quote: GILGIT: The federal interior ministry has imposed a ban on visits of foreign tourists to Gilgit-Baltistan without obtaining a no-objection certificate (NOC) from the ministry in Islamabad. A letter recently sent by the ministry to the Gilgit-Baltistan government says that it has been reported that foreigners are frequently visiting Gilgit-Baltistan without obtaining an NOC or security clearance from the ministry, which is against the rules. The letter asks the authorities concerned to take concrete measures to curb the practice.
end_quote: ISLAMABAD: Interior Minister Chaudhry Nisar Ali Khan on Thursday said that condition – which was made mandatory for foreign tourists – to have No-Objection Certificate (NOC) for visiting Gilgit-Baltistan has been lifted after holding meetings and forming consensus including with Chief Minister of the region, ARY News reported.
in_force_quote: Chaudhry also shared a notification from the Ministry of Interior which stated that as per cabinet decision dated January 31, 2019, "Free movement of foreigners shall be allowed in open cantonments except prohibited and restricted areas with visible signboards. The border crossings will be open and non-restricted."
found_via: seed (Dawn 2019 lead) -> search: Pakistan NOC foreigners Gilgit-Baltistan imposed interior ministry withdrawn 2017
notes: Dawn 2017-04-28 reports the ban (letter 'recently sent'; exact day not given; the letter calls visiting without NOC 'against the rules', i.e. enforcement of an older rule whose start is unsourced). ARY 2017-05-11 (Thursday) reports it lifted. Separately, on 2019-03-26 the government announced the end of the NOC regime country-wide: AJK, GB and Chitral 'non-restricted/non-prohibited' except border belts (10 miles Pak-China and Wakhan, 5 miles along the LoC, 10 miles Siachen) per Geo/Business Recorder citing an Interior Ministry notification under a cabinet decision of 2019-01-31. The older AJK/Chitral NOC regime has no sourced start date, so no separate row. No reinstatement found. in_force quote is the 2019 text, not a 2026 reading.

name: Visa-free visits to Chukotka by indigenous residents of Alaska
scope: Chukotka Autonomous Okrug
rule: Indigenous Alaskans invited by relatives may visit Chukotka without a visa for up to 90 days.
start_quote: The agreement was signed between USSR and United States on 23 September 1989 but came into force on 17 July 2015 after ratification by the United States.
notes: CONTRADICTS SEED wording ('1989 agreement; renewed 2015'): the pinned page says it came into force only on 2015-07-17. Status after 2022 not established; the page still lists it in the present tense, which is not evidence of operation.

name: Russian Far East e-visa (Free Port of Vladivostok, later Far Eastern Federal District)
scope: Far Eastern Federal District regions (Primorsky Krai first)
rule: Citizens of listed countries may enter on a free single-entry e-visa valid only for the named region(s) (up to 8 days).
start_quote: From 8 August 2017, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Russia started to implement the eVisa Program. Citizens of 18 countries could apply for an eVisa to visit regions in the Far Eastern Federal District
end_quote: The issuance of Russian electronic visas for the Far East District, Kaliningrad Oblast, and St Petersburg and Leningrad has been suspended since 18th March 2020 and has not been resumed yet.
in_force_quote: Электронная виза действительна для поездок по всей территории Российской Федерации.
notes: Not resumed as a regional scheme: the page of Nov 2020 says the regional programme 'will be valid until 1 January 2021' (legal replacement by a unified e-visa), and ru.wikipedia says the unified e-visa launch was postponed by the pandemic and started on 2023-08-01. end_date is the de-facto stop (COVID suspension); the formal end is the replacement by the national e-visa (2021-01-01 in law). No passage found on whether the scheme had a stated end date when it started, so that field is empty. Primary texts (mid.ru, Government Decree 595/2019, Presidential Decree 347/2019) not read.

name: Russia 72-hour visa-free stay for ferry (and cruise) passengers
scope: Listed port cities (stay limited to the tour programme area)
rule: Tourists arriving by regular ferry or cruise ship at listed ports may stay visa-free for up to 72 hours within the programme area.
start_quote: Since May 2009 international tourists entering by regular ferry via several ports have been able to stay in Russia visa-free for up to 72 hours, provided that they spend the night on-board or in accommodation specifically approved by the travel agency.
in_force_quote: International tourists entering by regular ferry via several ports are able to stay in Russia visa-free for up to 72 hours, provided that they spend the night on-board or in accommodation specifically approved by the travel agency.
notes: Port-list artefact rather than a named territory. 'In force' is the present-tense wording of the pinned 2026 Wikipedia revision; practical operation after 2020/2022 not verified (ferry lines to St Petersburg stopped - unverified).

name: Kaliningrad 72-hour tourist visa issued at the border ('experiment')
scope: Kaliningrad Oblast (Khrabrovo airport, Bagrationovsk and Mamonovo crossings)
rule: Foreign tourists could obtain a 72-hour visa at the border of Kaliningrad Oblast instead of applying at a consulate.
start_quote: с 2002 по 2017 год иностранные туристы из стран Шенгенской зоны, Великобритании и Японии могли получить краткосрочную визу на 72 часа при пересечении границы Калининградской области в автомобильных пунктах пропуска «Багратионовск» и «Мамоново», а также в аэропорту Храброво.
end_quote: starting from January 1, 2017 the MFA of Russia stops the experiment on issuing short-term 72 hours tourist visas to foreign nationals and stateless person crossing the border of the region.
expiry_quote: starting from January 1, 2017 the MFA of Russia stops the experiment on issuing short-term 72 hours tourist visas
in_force_quote: starting from January 1, 2017 the MFA of Russia stops the experiment on issuing short-term 72 hours tourist visas
notes: Start year from Kommersant (2019), which also confirms the end: 'С 1 января 2017 года эксперимент было решено прекратить'. ru.wikipedia (pinned) says visas at the border are issued under a government resolution 'с февраля 2002 года'; a search snippet says 1 Feb 2002 - the resolution itself was not read. 'Pilot' rests on the word 'experiment' in both sources; whether it had a stated end date at the start is not established. A search snippet (RBC, 2014-12-09, not fetchable) reports an earlier cancellation announced for 2015-01-01, apparently reversed - unverified.

name: Kaliningrad Oblast e-visa
scope: Kaliningrad Oblast
rule: Citizens of listed countries may enter on a free single-entry e-visa valid only for the named region(s) (up to 8 days).
start_quote: From 1 July 2019, in accordance with the Decree of the Government of the Russian Federation No. 595/2019, citizens of 54 countries could apply for single-entry business, humanitarian and tourist visas to visit Kaliningrad region.
end_quote: The issuance of Russian electronic visas for the Far East District, Kaliningrad Oblast, and St Petersburg and Leningrad has been suspended since 18th March 2020 and has not been resumed yet.
in_force_quote: Электронная виза действительна для поездок по всей территории Российской Федерации.
notes: Not resumed as a regional scheme: the page of Nov 2020 says the regional programme 'will be valid until 1 January 2021' (legal replacement by a unified e-visa), and ru.wikipedia says the unified e-visa launch was postponed by the pandemic and started on 2023-08-01. end_date is the de-facto stop (COVID suspension); the formal end is the replacement by the national e-visa (2021-01-01 in law). No passage found on whether the scheme had a stated end date when it started, so that field is empty. Primary texts (mid.ru, Government Decree 595/2019, Presidential Decree 347/2019) not read.

name: Poland-Russia local border traffic (Kaliningrad Oblast)
scope: Kaliningrad Oblast (and listed Polish border counties on the other side)
rule: Residents of the Polish border area holding a local border traffic permit may visit Kaliningrad Oblast without a visa.
start_quote: From 27 July 2012, residents of the border areas of Poland who have a permit for local border traffic can visit Kaliningrad Oblast without a visa.
end_quote: The agreement has been suspended for an indefinite period by Poland from 4 July 2016.
in_force_quote: Poland has suspended the border traffic agreements with Russia indefinitely from 4 July 2016.
found_via: enwiki 'Visa policy of Russia', section on border areas (beyond seed)
notes: Suspension was announced as temporary (NATO summit / World Youth Day) per general reporting - not read; never resumed according to the pinned Wikipedia pages. Regime applies to border residents only, not to travellers in general.

name: Visa-free visits of Japanese citizens to the southern Kuril Islands (1991 and 1999 agreements)
scope: Kunashir, Iturup and the Lesser Kuril chain (Sakhalin Oblast)
rule: Japanese former residents, their families and exchange groups could visit the islands without passports/visas under a special procedure.
start_quote: It terminates the agreement between the foreign ministers of the former Soviet Union and Japan on the procedure of mutual trips of October 14, 1991
end_quote: MOSCOW, September 5. /TASS/. Russia has withdrawn from the agreement with Japan on simplified visiting the Kuril Islands by Japanese nationals, former residents of these territories and from the agreement of the procedure of mutual trips.
in_force_quote: Russia has withdrawn from the agreement with Japan on simplified visiting the Kuril Islands by Japanese nationals
found_via: own lead (ended regional regimes in Russia); web search: Russia terminates visa-free visits Kuril 2022
notes: Start date is the date of the 1991 agreement (first visits 1992 - unverified); a second agreement of 1999-09-02 covered former residents. End date is the TASS dateline; search snippets give 3 Sept 2022 for the resolution - not in a fetched passage. Visits had already stopped in 2020 (COVID) per general reporting - unverified. Disputed territory. Started before 2000.

name: Latvia-Russia local border traffic zone
scope: Listed border municipalities of Latvia and of Pskov Oblast
rule: Border-area residents with a local border traffic permit may visit the other side's border area without a visa.
start_quote: As of June 2017 [update] , ten local-traffic agreements have come into force. Hungary–Ukraine from January 2008. Slovakia–Ukraine from September 2008. Poland–Ukraine in July 2009. Romania–Moldova from October 2010. Latvia–Belarus from February 2012. Norway–Russia from May 2012. Poland–Russia (Kaliningrad Area) from July 2012 (suspended since July 2016) Latvia–Russia from June 2013.
end_quote: The Latvian government has decided to suspend its agreement with Russia, which simplifies mutual visits by residents of border territories, from August 1, the BNS news agency reported on Thursday.
found_via: enwiki 'Schengen Area' list; web search: Latvia Russia local border traffic suspended
notes: Interfax report dated 14 Jul 2022. No source read on whether the agreement was later resumed or denounced; the current enwiki 'Visa policy of Russia' still describes it in the present tense, which conflicts with the suspension - in_force left empty. Applies to border residents only.

name: Norilsk industrial area closed to foreigners
scope: Norilsk, Talnakh, Kayerkan, Dudinka, Igarka (Krasnoyarsk Krai)
rule: Foreign citizens need special permission to visit; Russian citizens do not.
start_quote: However, on 30 October 2001, foreign travel was restricted without exception in the northern cities of Norilsk , Talnakh , Kayerkan , Dudinka , and Igarka .
in_force_quote: Norilsk remains a closed city , and foreign citizens require special permission to visit the area.
found_via: enwiki 'Closed city' (looking for areas restricted after 2000)
notes: Wikipedia only; the government act of 2001 not read (another common date for entry into force is 25 Nov 2001 - unverified).

name: Norway-Russia local border traffic zone
scope: 30 km border zone: parts of Pechengsky District (RU) and Sør-Varanger (NO)
rule: Border-area residents with a local border traffic permit may cross and stay in the other side's border zone without a visa.
start_quote: As of June 2017 [update] , ten local-traffic agreements have come into force. Hungary–Ukraine from January 2008. Slovakia–Ukraine from September 2008. Poland–Ukraine in July 2009. Romania–Moldova from October 2010. Latvia–Belarus from February 2012. Norway–Russia from May 2012.
